scope.review_method: Counts and expected-target equality computed across all 71 clean/audit rejections. The listed semantic examples are spot checks, not a full independent adjudication of all 71; unlisted cases remain unconfirmed.

interpretation.audit_review: All 38 audit-rejected targets exactly equal expected_clean and all have meaning_preserved=true. 32 have a source_valid issue; 28 of those also have cleanup_complete=true, while four have cleanup_complete=false. Manual source/target spot checks (three examples below) show explicit final corrections that support the target, so source_valid false raises a false-reject suspicion; the records do not prove the audit is wrong. Four records have cleanup issues (one overlaps source_valid); three others fail target-clean/exactness with no reported issues. Do not count all 38 as confirmed false rejections.
interpretation.clean_review: All 33 clean rejections have teacher responses in api_calls.jsonl and none is a transport failure. Several clearly retain abandoned correction content, emit the spoken repair marker in the target, or omit/alter final content. Other observed discrepancies are formatting/paraphrase-level and are not counted as confirmed semantic errors without adjudication.
interpretation.construction_alignment: At least one clear alignment concern: scale_daily_chat_0068 has expected_clean “网红餐厅排队技巧其实关键在于错峰和提前预约。” while oral construction ends with “不对，避开高峰时段，最后改成，错峰和提前预约。” The teacher’s paraphrase preserves the apparent intent but fails the exact target; this should be treated as a construction/target alignment candidate, not a confirmed teacher recovery error. Similar target-vs-oral review is warranted before attributing every clean mismatch to the teacher.
